_doc: Overlay timeline for the final cut (absolute seconds; frame f shows time f/24).
Resolved by comp/overlays.py into a per-frame timeline (word refs -> exact word times from timing/shots.json,
tracker JSON -> smoothed screen paths) and rendered by comp/overlay/overlay.js in headless Chromium.
Word refs: {"shot": .., "word": .., "nth": k} = start time of the k-th occurrence of that word in that shot,
minus 'lead' seconds (the eye leads the ear by ~1-2 frames). Any time may instead be a number (absolute s), or
{"word": .., "abs": t}: absolute, but still naming its narrated word (hold/exit checks, key-word identity in the sync sheet).
Key-word timing rule (final-fix pass): a word is READABLE (half its edge contrast drawn, first word of a multi-word line)
~0.05-0.15 s before its voice onset in voice_proc.wav, never more than ~0.2 s early (the transcript starts absorb the pauses).
Keyword 'out' = the moment the short exit (0.25-0.3 s) has fully finished. Optional keyword 'scrim': {from, to, k[, fade]}
= a soft dark vignette (strength k, 'fade' 0.15 s eases inside [from, to], gated by the word's alpha) behind the line,
a floor on the compositor's legibility darkening (edit.json finish.legibility.scrim sets its shape). overlays.py --resolve checks every key word:
settled hold (all letters legible) >= 0.8 s, exit only after the last word has been spoken, gone by the cut (+2 frames)
unless a 'carry' reason is given, one key word in the band at a time, ink inside the safe area (rendered extents).
Callout 'sync' = the moment the anchor dot lands (UI tick in the sound mix); 'out' = fully gone. Callout options:
'leader' (px), 'follow' (fraction of the anchor motion the label follows), 'clamp' (anchor glides to a stop this many
px inside the safe area instead of fading), 'enabled'. Trackers come from comp/tracks/<shot>.json (export_tracks
format); 'fallback' is used when that file / tracker is missing (static [x, y] or keys [[t, x, y], ...]).
Safe area (BRIEF §3/§5): key words in band y 520-820, nothing below y 1498 (bottom 22%), x > 950 (right 12%)
